Marissa — reviewed the redlines. High-level legal assessment and recommended positions below (see attached "Redwood_response_summary.pdf" for line-by-line):

1) Liability cap 
- BrightCloud: unlimited or very high cap for service failures.
- Redwood recommendation: keep cap tied to fees (standard: greater of 12 months' fees or $3M floor). We can consider a higher cap for specific SOWs if commercial is willing to add insurance/fees.

2) Indemnity
- Make IP indemnity unilateral for IP infringement (we accept claims against our tech, mutual for third-party claims). Carve out liabilities caused by customer data misuse.

3) DPA / Audit Rights
- Reject broad, unlimited audit rights. Offer: documented security questionnaires + an annual SOC 2 report plus ad-hoc audits only for cause with 30 days' notice and scoped to the alleged issue. Data deletion timeline: 90 days post-termination with limited retention for legal obligations.

4) Subprocessors / Transfer
- Accept subprocessors with prior notice and a right to object for legitimate security reasons. Include standard SCCs for EU data.

5) SLA and Remedies
- Push back on financial remedies that are uncapped. Offer service credits as remedy with clear uptime measurement windows.

6) SOW acceptance and payment
- Agree to acceptance criteria in SOW but keep 30-day acceptance window and net-30 payment. If BrightCloud needs PO-first, commercial can consider a partial milestone invoice to secure kickoff.

Next steps I recommend:
- Marissa: send the partner a consolidated counter with the positions above and attach our proposed redlines (Proposed_MSADPA_SOW_counter.docx).
- If BrightCloud insists on higher cap or unlimited audit, schedule a legal call; prepare justification for any commercial concessions (revenue, strategic value).

I attached a short redline summary and the recommended counter-document. Happy to join the call.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are Redwood’s consolidated positions and our proposed counter-document (Proposed_MSADPA_SOW_counter.docx and Redwood_response_summary.pdf). Summary of the positions we can accept and where we need modest changes: 

1) Liability
- We cannot accept unlimited liability. Our standard position: liability capped at the greater of (i) fees paid under the SOW(s) in the preceding 12 months and (ii) $3,000,000. If BrightCloud requires a higher cap for this deal, we can discuss an SOW-level uplift tied to additional insurance and a commercial premium.

2) Indemnity
- Mutual indemnity with Redwood indemnifying for IP infringement; carveouts included for Customer misuse of the service.

3) DPA / Audit
- We will provide SOC 2 Type II and complete security questionnaire. We cannot agree to unlimited onsite audits. We can accept an annual third-party audit and ad-hoc audits for cause (with 30 days' notice and scope limited to the issue). Data retention/deletion: 90 days post-termination. EU transfers covered by SCCs.

4) SLA / Remedies
- We will commit to uptime metrics and service credits as the exclusive financial remedy. No open-ended penalty structure.

5) SOW / Commercial
- We agree the SOW scope and timeline in principle. BrightCloud’s procurement notes: PO-before-kickoff is standard for you — we can accept that but request a partial invoice (50%) upon countersignature to reserve capacity, remainder net-30 after acceptance. Kickoff target: March 1, 2026 assuming countersigned docs and PO.

Can you confirm if those positions are acceptable? If yes, we’ll route the documents for DocuSign and provide a PO template for BrightCloud to return. If you prefer a legal call, propose two slots this week and Lauren will join.

Best,
Marissa
